decision_note: Primary/secondary nectar robbing is the experimental exposure; no independent floral attraction coordinate A is evaluated as a shared receiver trait.
Callistemon floral-biology survey records visitors and nectar theft but does not link pollinator and antagonist responses to one declared floral A.

A_trait: flower size and flower number
claim_ceiling: Same attractiveness traits predict both receiver classes and opposing selection, but A is not randomized.
decision_note: Collaea cipoensis: larger/more flowers increased both pollinator and antagonist visits; floral antagonists reduced female fitness and counteracted pollinator-mediated selection.
Tree-species dissertation describes floral visitors; the retained florivore keyword does not resolve a focal plant-antagonist response to a shared floral coordinate.
Zieria study resolves floral biology pollination vectors and breeding system without a focal plant-antagonist receiver response.
Floral Evolution: Breeding Systems Pollinators and Beyond is an editorial/synthesis rather than an independent primary study.

A_trait: floral tissue integrity / artificial florivory level
claim_ceiling: Artificial floral damage is a causal A perturbation with pollination and fitness outcomes, but the antagonist is the antecedent manipulation rather than a receiver response to A.
decision_note: Royal irises: low/high artificial florivory did not significantly change pollen deposition fruit set or seed set.
Fifty-year floral-nectar review is useful source-chasing material but is not an independent primary report.

A_trait: symmetric floral nectar-guide pattern
claim_ceiling: Same manipulated visual pattern changes legitimate-versus-robbing behavior, but there is no plant reproductive outcome.
decision_note: Artificial-flower nectar-guide experiment directly tests role allocation by bumblebees on the same visual coordinate.
Floral-phytochemistry article is a synthesis of VOC/nectar effects rather than an independent primary shared-cue experiment.

A_trait: flower abundance morphology colour scent nectar and pollen
claim_ceiling: Herbivore species causally alter floral traits and pollinator behavior, but the herbivores are antecedents rather than receivers of the resulting A.
decision_note: Brassica nigra: six herbivore species induce species-specific floral changes with positive negative or neutral pollinator responses.

A_trait: anthocyanin floret-spot floral morph
claim_ceiling: Pollinators and florivores track the same floral morph with opposing consequences, but the morph is not randomized in a common plant-fitness experiment.
decision_note: Ursinia calenduliflora: spotted morph attracts effective pollinators but incurs greater ovule predation; spatially structured polymorphism and visitor composition support context-dependent antagonistic selection.
Whole-plant floral-scent article is a synthesis/review and is not counted as an independent primary study.
Metrioptera feeding trials measure florivore deterrence by floral scent compounds; pollinator responses to those compounds are prior-literature context rather than measured in this report.

A_trait: corolla tube length flower number and nectar traits
claim_ceiling: Trait associations and robber exclusion link attraction robbing and seed production, but A itself is not randomized.
decision_note: Caryopteris: short tubes reduce robbing and increase legitimate visitation/seed production; long tubes are preferred by robbers.
Impatiens study identifies pollinators a nectar robber and reproduction but does not test how one floral attraction coordinate drives both receiver classes.

A_trait: nectar sexual dimorphism and water-calyx defensive architecture
claim_ceiling: Different floral components support pollinator attraction and herbivore defence; this is functional partitioning not a same-A conflict test or historical shared-to-private transition.
decision_note: Chrysothemis dissertation: nectar dimorphism tests pollinator/sexual-selection functions while the water calyx experimentally protects buds from microlepidopteran herbivory.

A_trait: flower size corolla traits and nectar reward
claim_ceiling: Floral traits legitimate pollination robber preference and female fitness occur in one study, but A is observational.
decision_note: Polygala vayredae: nectar drives legitimate pollination; flower size predicts robbing in one population and robbing-pollination correlations vary among populations.

A_trait: floral morphology nectar production and display
claim_ceiling: Pollinator and robber roles share the same flowers and reproductive context, but no single floral A is experimentally manipulated.
decision_note: Drymonia species: morphology/nectar legitimate pollinator visits nectar robbers and fruit-set/breeding outcomes are measured in the same study.

A_trait: floral morphology reward and visitor access
claim_ceiling: Pollinator and robber roles are quantified with reproduction, but response to one manipulated A is not identified.
decision_note: Impatiens chinensis: Bombus is the dominant pollinator and Amegilla nectar robbing is identified as an important influence on sexual reproduction.
The V18 preprint resolves to the Sasidharan et al. cross-study review/meta-analysis of pollinator and florivore responses not an independent primary system.

A_trait: floral outline colour scent and nectar after florivory
claim_ceiling: Artificial florivory changes corolla outline but does not discourage hummingbird pollination; antagonist response to the altered A is not measured.
decision_note: Pyrostegia venusta: most visual/chemical/reward traits were unchanged by florivory; altered outline had neutral pollination effect.

A_trait: floral tissue damage / display integrity
claim_ceiling: Causal floral-damage test informs florivory-to-pollination coupling, but the florivore is not a receiver responding to A.
decision_note: Mimulus artificial-damage experiment is retained as an induced-state near-pass with a null/weak pollinator-visitation effect.

A_trait: petal presence and flower size
claim_ceiling: Petal damage causally reduces pollinator-mediated reproductive output, but no antagonist response to the manipulated floral A is measured.
decision_note: Eurya japonica: petal removal reduced natural fruit/seed set but not artificially pollinated output; flower size increased visitor numbers.

A_trait: floral attractive traits after florivory
claim_ceiling: Florivory causally alters floral traits/interactions and reproduction, but does not close a same-A two-receiver response.
decision_note: Impatiens capensis experiment manipulates floral damage and measures attractive traits floral interactions and plant reproduction.
Tanacetum chemotype experiments measure florivore attraction and floral chemistry; pollinator relevance is framing rather than a measured pollinator response in this report.

A_trait: floral terpenoid chemotype and plot-level chemodiversity
claim_ceiling: Pollinators and florivores respond to floral chemotype/chemodiversity and pollinator visits predict germination, but floral chemistry is not randomized at the individual chemical coordinate.
decision_note: Tanacetum preprint: heterogeneous plots receive more pollinators florivore visits depend on chemotype and germination correlates positively with pollinator visits.

A_trait: flower number / floral display
claim_ceiling: Many-flowered plants amplify both visitor classes and antagonists dominate the network, but display is not randomized.
decision_note: Collaea cipoensis network: many-flowered plants are more central/visited mainly via antagonists; hummingbirds contribute pollination quality but centrality does not raise reproductive success.
Cleistocactus study quantifies pollinator dependence and floral larceny but does not identify a shared floral A whose variation is evaluated against both roles.

A_trait: flowerhead density after foliar herbivory
claim_ceiling: Herbivory reduces flowerhead density and indirectly visitor-network centrality, but the herbivore is antecedent rather than a receiver of A.
decision_note: Foliar herbivory reduces flowerhead density and indirectly Hymenoptera visitation/network centrality.

A_trait: individual floral fragrance compounds
claim_ceiling: Several identical floral compounds attract both pollinators and floral herbivores, but no plant reproductive outcome is measured.
decision_note: Cirsium arvense: benzaldehyde and phenylacetaldehyde attracted both pollinators and floral herbivores in scent-baited traps.

A_trait: corolla exsertion lower-lip length and floral display traits
claim_ceiling: Floral traits covary with pollination benefit and seed-predation cost across populations, but A is observational.
decision_note: Pedicularis rex: floral morphology predicts pollen load and seed predation yielding geographically variable conflicting selection.

A_trait: flower size
claim_ceiling: Flower size covaries geographically with pollinator size/composition and nectar-robbing regime, but A is observational and common plant fitness is not measured.
decision_note: Lamium/Meehania: local flower size tracks visitor composition; one Meehania population with predominant nectar robbing has uniquely small flowers.

A_trait: plant height flower number and floral resistance/attraction traits
claim_ceiling: Regional genotypes differ in robbing resistance pollinator attraction and reproduction; the implicated A traits are not independently randomized.
decision_note: Gelsemium: northern genotypes are less robbed but receive about half the pollinator visits and have lower reproduction consistent with a geographic resistance-attraction trade-off.
Rhododendron study measures grayanotoxin chemistry across tissues/species; current pollinator and herbivore behavioral responses to the floral chemical coordinate are not measured.

A_trait: flower number morphology and scent after herbivory/demethylation
claim_ceiling: Causally altered floral signaling changes pollinator attractiveness, but antagonist response to the resulting A and common W are not measured.
decision_note: Brassica rapa: herbivory changes floral methylation/phenotype; standardized demethylation reduces flower morphology/scent and Bombus attractiveness.

A_trait: flower number display and flowering start date
claim_ceiling: Strong geographic antagonist-mediated selection on floral traits, but no paired pollinator response to the same A is measured.
decision_note: Primula florindae: experimentally estimated herbivore-mediated selection on floral display varies nonlinearly with herbivory intensity among 11 populations.

A_trait: distylous floral traits and gelsemine-associated visitor traits
claim_ceiling: Pollinator and nectar-robber interactions are linked to floral/resistance traits, but the shared A is observational and common W is not closed.
decision_note: Gelsemium sempervirens study tests correlations among distyly secondary compounds and interactions with pollinators/nectar robbers.

A_trait: floral sex ratio
claim_ceiling: Herbivores alter selection on an important reproductive trait, but paired pollinator response to the same A is not measured.
decision_note: Solanum carolinense: increasing flower/fruit herbivory shifts selection on floral-sex ratio from stabilizing toward fewer male flowers.

A_trait: inflorescence number flower size and reproductive traits
claim_ceiling: Factorial manipulation identifies herbivore/pollinator-mediated selection on reproductive traits but does not measure both receivers reading one manipulated A.
decision_note: Trifolium repens: cyanogenesis herbivore suppression and pollination are factorially manipulated; herbivores impose stronger selection on reproductive traits than pollinators.

A_trait: floral VOC emission and flower number after herbivory
claim_ceiling: Herbivory causally alters floral scent pollinator attraction and seed production, but the antagonist is an antecedent and parasitoid attraction is indirect defence rather than plant antagonism.
decision_note: Brassica rapa: herbivory reduces floral VOCs/pollinator attraction changes flower production and can reduce seed production.

A_trait: herbivore-induced defence floral morphometry and floral volatiles
claim_ceiling: Replicated evolutionary selection regimes alter induced defence/floral plasticity, but the study does not close a contemporary same-A dual-receiver fitness surface.
decision_note: Fast-cycling Brassica rapa evolved for six generations under bee/hand pollination × herbivory selection treatments.
Herbivory changes pollen chemistry and bee-pathogen infection outcomes but bees are assayed as pathogen hosts rather than as a pollination-service response to a floral A.
Phloem-feeding herbivory suppresses floral volatile production; the current study does not directly measure pollinator response to the altered floral volatiles.

A_trait: herbivore-induced floral volatiles
claim_ceiling: Synthetic addition supports a causal floral-scent-to-pollination pathway, but no antagonist response to those same volatiles is measured.
decision_note: Silene latifolia: herbivory increases two floral volatiles; adding them to undamaged flowers increases fruit production with nocturnal pollination.

A_trait: olfactory visual and nectar traits of flowers after jasmonate treatment
claim_ceiling: Herbivory-induced floral/EFN traits causally alter pollinator foraging, but no focal antagonist response to the resulting floral A is measured.
decision_note: Vicia faba: jasmonate shifts floral/EFN scent visual and nectar traits so Bombus loses its control preference for flowers over EFNs.
